lines.text: What if, starting tomorrow, you could see when ANYONE is lying?
Not a guess. Not a feeling... A number. Floating right above their head.
Zero means the truth... A hundred means… well. You'll see.
At first, it feels like the best thing that's ever happened to you... It isn't. But we'll get there.
You wake up. Your alarm says "five more minutes won't hurt."... Eighty-two percent.
Downstairs, Mom says breakfast is "almost ready." Thirty-one percent. Fair.
Your little brother says he did NOT eat the last cookie... Ninety-nine.
The rules are simple. The meter only shows up when someone talks. It glows gold when they're honest… and red when they're not.
It works on people, on ads, on the cereal box that says "part of a balanced breakfast."... SEVENTY-FOUR.
On the bus, the driver says he'll "wait just one more minute." Ninety. He does not wait.
A guy on a billboard promises you'll "lose ten pounds in a week."... The meter is so red, it's basically on fire.
By lunch, you've figured out the first big secret... Almost nobody lies to hurt you. They lie to make things EASIER. Mostly for themselves.
At school, it's basically a cheat code.
"This won't be on the test." Ninety-one. You study that chapter twice.
"I totally didn't copy your homework." Hundred. You knew that one already.
At the school's casino night fundraiser, the guy running the card table says the deck is "totally random."... Sixty-eight.
You don't win money. The chips are fake... But you win EVERY hand. And people start to notice.
Suddenly, everyone wants you on their team. For group projects. For debates. For "is he into me?"
For about a week,... you're the most popular kid in school.
You settle arguments. "Did she REALLY say that about me?"... Twelve percent. Drama over.
You catch the class rumor before it spreads. You know which compliments are real, and which ones are just polite.
And honestly?... You start to think, you might be the only person in the world, who sees things CLEARLY.
Then it starts showing you things you didn't ask for.
Your best friend says, "No, I'm not mad."... Fifty-five.
Your teacher says, "Everyone gets a fair chance." Forty.
Your dad, on the phone, late at night: "Everything's fine. Don't worry about it."... Eighty-eight.
You start hearing people differently. Every "I'm good,", every "no worries,", every "love you"… comes with a number.
And numbers don't care how you feel.
You stop asking questions. Because you're scared of the answers.
At dinner, everyone talks, and you just watch the numbers float, over the mashed potatoes.
Maya texts you, "we're good, right?"... Texts don't have meters... And for some reason, that's worse.
You realise you don't trust anyone anymore... Not because they changed. Because YOU did.
One night, you can't sleep. You go to the bathroom, look in the mirror, and say it out loud.
"I'm fine."
Ninety-six.
Turns out, the person lying the most, wasn't your friend. Or your dad. Or the card dealer.
It was you. To yourself. Every single day.
And here's the thing the meter never told you... It shows THAT someone is lying... Not WHY.
Your friend wasn't hiding anger. She was hurt... Your dad wasn't hiding a lie. He was protecting you.
Even your little brother, wasn't lying about the cookie to be evil... He just really, really, likes cookies.
A lie, it turns out, is usually a door someone closed, because they didn't know how to open it.
So the next morning, you do something new.
You ask your dad what's really going on. And you listen.
Some meters go down. Some stay high... But for the first time, you're not reading numbers. You're reading people.
You don't text Maya. Not "we're good, right?"... You call her. You say sorry. And you mean it... No meter needed.
That night, you look in the mirror again. "I'm not fine. But I will be."... Zero.
So, if you could see when anyone is lying… would you WANT to?
Tell me in the comments. I'll know if you're honest... Zero percent. Probably.
